description.value: The study examined whether simple multiplication processing differs between the language in which bilingual adults learned multiplication and their other language, using behavioral measures and fMRI.

spans.text: For question 1, we compared the languages collapsed across problem size (i.e., “LA+ [all problems – control] > LA- [all problems – control]” and “LA- [all problems – control] > LA+ [all problems – control].”)

design.value: Thirty-five Spanish-English bilingual adults completed verbal and numerosity localizer tasks and a single-digit multiplication verification task in English and Spanish during fMRI; six participants were excluded, leaving 29 participants for analysis.
